title: Steve Jobs 1994: why to start young, build what you need, and remember life was made up by people no smarter than you
summary: In a 1994 interview, Jobs explains how Apple grew out of Silicon Valley's values, blue boxes and the Homebrew Club. He argues for acting young with nothing to lose, building for yourself, asking boldly, and learning that the world can be changed.

principles.text: Start young, when you have nothing to lose; the experience is worth far more than the cost.
principles.quote: We figured even if we crash and burn and lose everything, the experience will have been worth 10 times the cost. So, what did we have to lose? There was no risk.

principles.text: Build the product you yourself want; being the customer lets you do both the design and the marketing.
principles.quote: We were building a product that we ourselves were the customer for. We were building something we wanted ourselves.

principles.text: Ask. Most people never pick up the phone, and that separates doers from dreamers.
principles.quote: Most people never pick up the phone and call. Most people never ask. And that's what separates sometimes the people that do things from the people that just dream about them.

principles.text: Be willing to fail; fear of failing stops you from getting far.
principles.quote: You've got to be willing to crash and burn, you know, with people on the phone, with starting a company, with whatever. If you're afraid of failing, you won't get very far.

principles.text: To see the future, watch the fringe, not the mainstream.
principles.quote: If you want to know what's going to happen in 5 years, you you don't look in the mainstream, you look at the fringe.

principles.text: Life was made up by people no smarter than you, and you can change it and make your mark on it.
principles.quote: everything around you that you call life was made up by people that were no smarter than you. And you can change it. You can influence it.
